item.title: 1. Personalised Headlines Tailored to You
item.description:
Personalised Headlines Tailored to You

The Idea

Every time we open a news app or scroll a social feed, someone has already made decisions about how to present what we see. The headline is rarely neutral. It has been optimised for engagement, for reach, for the emotional reaction most likely to make us stop scrolling.

What most people do not realise is how precise that optimisation can be. Not just “make it sound urgent” or “make it sound alarming”, but calibrated to specific psychological signals like political identity, current emotional state, level of institutional trust, how we typically respond when a headline challenges something we already believe etc.

item.title: 2. Rethinking How Product Teams Prioritise
item.description:
Rethinking How Product Teams Prioritise

The Challenge

Product Managers face the ongoing challenge of ruthless prioritisation throughout the product lifecycle.

For Product Managers, ruthless prioritisation is a constant balancing act, making tough calls while ensuring every decision stays true to the product vision.

item.title: 3. What If Property Search Actually Used the Photos?
item.description:
What If Property Search Actually Used the Photos?

The Challenge

Property search has not fundamentally changed in years. Platforms let you filter by bedrooms, price, and location, but the photos, which are often the first and most influential thing a prospective renter or buyer looks at, play no role in how listings are filtered or ranked.

item.title: 4. Skipping the Part Clients Hate
item.description:
Skipping the Part Clients Hate

The Challenge

Cloud migrations rarely fail in the execution. They fail before they begin.

Consulting companies specialising in Cloud migrations often face challenges when clients resist paying for initial Cloud assessment. The main issue stems from the perception that the assessment is an “additional cost” with no immediate value to the core goal of migration, which is the transfer of the applications to the Cloud.

item.title: 5. The Diagram That Takes Three Days to Draw
item.description:
The Diagram That Takes Three Days to Draw

The Challenge

Understanding how value moves through an organisation requires talking to people. Teams conduct rounds of interviews across departments, gathering perspectives on how work flows, who depends on whom, and where things slow down or break down.

item.title: 6. What Happens When Two AIs Talk to Each Other?
item.description:
What Happens When Two AIs Talk to Each Other?

The Idea

Most AI interactions follow the same pattern: a human asks, a model responds. Agents Duo flips that. The human steps back after the setup, choosing the models, configuring their personalities, picking a topic or letting the agents choose one themselves, and then lets the conversation run.

item.title: 7. Technology and Product Modernisation
item.description:
Technology and Product Modernisation

Challenges

Many organisations struggle with the limitations of outdated technologies and legacy products that hinder their ability to scale, innovate and remain competitive. These challenges often present themselves in various areas, including operational inefficiencies, suboptimal customer experience and increased costs for maintenance and integration. These challenges are compounded by misaligned strategies, technical debt, and resistance to change within organisations.

item.title: 8. Product Transformation and Delivery
item.description:
Product Transformation and Delivery

Challenges

Across industries many organisations struggle with legacy product structures and ways of working that hinder their ability to adopt new technologies and innovate at scale. These challenges are particularly relevant to industries where agility and operational efficiency are critical to maintain a competitive edge, like financial services and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: 9. An AI With One Job, Make You Smile
item.description:
An AI With One Job, Make You Smile

The Idea

There are thousands of AI chatbots. Almost none of them are trying to make you laugh.

That felt like a gap worth poking at. Not because the world urgently needs more dad jokes, it does not, but because designing for humour as a primary goal turned out to be a genuinely interesting constraint. Helpful is easy to optimise for. Funny is much harder to define, and even harder to sustain across a full conversation.
